references.text: Levi and Simeon avenge their sister Dinah by attacking the city of Shechem. This event reveals Levi's character and has consequences for the tribe's future.

Jacob prophesies over Levi and Simeon that they will be scattered in Israel because of their violence. For Levi, this was fulfilled when the Levites were dispersed among all the tribes as temple servants.
Levi is mentioned among Jacob's sons who came to Egypt, showing the tribe's continued significance in Israel's history.
Levi's sons—Gershon, Kohath, and Merari—are named as founders of the three main branches of the Levites.
The Levites are to 'join' (Hebrew: yillavu) Aaron in temple service—a wordplay connecting to Leah's words in Gen 29:34 that her husband will now 'join' (yillaveh) her.
The tribe of Levi was set apart by the Lord to carry the ark of the covenant and stand before the Lord to serve him, giving Levi's naming a deeper meaning.
Parallel account of Leah's naming based on hope for marital recognition through fertility.
Contrast between Rachel's focus on God's justice and Leah's focus on her husband's love in naming their sons.
Continuity in the motif of sons as a means to win favor with both God and husband in the cases of Leah and Rachel.
Direct continuation of the same narrative about Leah's fertility and naming.
